title: The Lucky Mould That Almost Went Nowhere
subtitle: 差點被遺忘的幸運黴菌：青黴素的真實故事
source: 原創議題文章；依 Wikipedia〈Alexander Fleming〉〈Penicillin〉〈History of penicillin〉〈Norman Heatley〉核對，2026-10-22

beginner.title: Mould on a Dish
paras: In September 1928, a Scottish scientist called Alexander Fleming came back to his laboratory in London after a holiday. Before he left, he had put some bacteria on small dishes. Now he saw something strange: mould was growing on one dish, and the bacteria around the mould were dead.
1928 年 9 月，蘇格蘭科學家亞歷山大．弗萊明度假回來，回到他在倫敦的實驗室。出發前，他在幾個小培養皿上放了一些細菌。現在他看到一件奇怪的事：其中一個培養皿長了黴菌，而黴菌周圍的細菌都死了。

Fleming realised that the mould made something that could kill bacteria. In 1929 he named it penicillin. He wrote about it in a science journal, but few people paid attention. He also could not make enough pure penicillin to use as a medicine.
弗萊明意識到，這種黴菌會產生能殺死細菌的東西。1929 年，他把它命名為青黴素（盤尼西林）。他把發現寫成論文發表在科學期刊上，卻沒什麼人注意。他也沒辦法製造出足夠的純青黴素來當藥用。

About ten years later, a team at the University of Oxford, led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain, started working on penicillin. In May 1940 they tested it on eight sick mice. The four mice without penicillin died. The four mice with penicillin were still alive the next day. Florey called it “a miracle”.
大約十年後，牛津大學一個由霍華德．弗洛里和恩斯特．柴恩帶領的團隊，開始研究青黴素。1940 年 5 月，他們用八隻生病的老鼠做測試。沒打青黴素的四隻老鼠死了，打了青黴素的四隻隔天都還活著。弗洛里稱之為「奇蹟」。

Making penicillin was very hard. The team grew mould in special pots shaped like hospital bedpans. In 1941 they treated a policeman with a terrible infection. He started to get better, but they ran out of penicillin, and he died. Later, factories learned to make much more. In 1942, one of the first American patients treated with penicillin used half of all the penicillin made in the country at that time.
製造青黴素非常困難。團隊用形狀像醫院便盆的特製陶罐培養黴菌。1941 年，他們治療了一位嚴重感染的警察。他開始好轉，但青黴素用完了，他還是過世了。後來，工廠學會了大量生產青黴素。1942 年，美國最早接受青黴素治療的病人之一，就用掉了當時全國生產的青黴素的一半。

In 1945, Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize. Today, many people remember only Fleming’s lucky discovery. But penicillin became a medicine because a whole team worked hard for years. Great discoveries often need both luck and teamwork.
1945 年，弗萊明、弗洛里和柴恩共同獲得諾貝爾獎。今天，很多人只記得弗萊明的幸運發現。但青黴素之所以能成為藥物，是因為整個團隊努力了好幾年。偉大的發現，往往同時需要運氣和團隊合作。

intermediate.title: The Lucky Mould That Almost Went Nowhere
paras: On 3 September 1928, Alexander Fleming returned to his laboratory at St Mary’s Hospital in London after a family holiday. Before leaving, he had left some dishes of staphylococcus bacteria on a bench. One had become contaminated with a mould, and the bacteria immediately around it had been destroyed. It is one of the most famous accidents in the history of science.
1928 年 9 月 3 日，亞歷山大．弗萊明結束家庭度假，回到倫敦聖瑪麗醫院的實驗室。出發前，他把幾個培養葡萄球菌的培養皿留在實驗桌上。其中一個被黴菌污染了，而黴菌周圍的細菌都被消滅了。這是科學史上最有名的意外之一。

Fleming investigated the “mould juice” and, on 7 March 1929, named its active substance penicillin. Yet the discovery nearly stalled. His paper in the British Journal of Experimental Pathology attracted little attention, and he was unsure about its medical use. Fleming did not abandon the work, as is sometimes claimed, but neither he nor his assistants managed to purify the substance in useful amounts.
弗萊明研究了這種「黴菌汁」，並在 1929 年 3 月 7 日把其中的有效物質命名為青黴素。然而，這項發現幾乎停滯不前。他發表在《英國實驗病理學期刊》的論文沒有引起太多注意，他自己也不確定它的醫療用途。弗萊明並沒有像某些說法那樣放棄這項研究，但他和助手都沒能把這種物質純化到可用的分量。

The breakthrough came from Oxford. From 1939, a team led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed ways to grow the mould, extract penicillin and measure its purity. On 25 May 1940, Florey infected eight mice with dangerous bacteria and gave penicillin to four of them. By the next morning, all four untreated mice were dead, while the treated mice were still alive. Florey described the result as “a miracle”. The team was also lucky in its choice of animals: penicillin is toxic to guinea pigs, so testing on them might have stopped the research.
突破來自牛津。從 1939 年起，由霍華德．弗洛里和恩斯特．柴恩帶領的團隊，發展出培養黴菌、萃取青黴素和測量純度的方法。1940 年 5 月 25 日，弗洛里讓八隻老鼠感染危險的細菌，再給其中四隻注射青黴素。到了隔天早上，四隻未治療的老鼠全死了，接受治療的老鼠卻都還活著。弗洛里形容這個結果是「奇蹟」。團隊在實驗動物的選擇上也很幸運：青黴素對天竺鼠有毒，如果拿天竺鼠測試，研究可能就此中斷。

Producing enough for humans was the next problem. The biochemist Norman Heatley realised that vessels shaped like hospital bedpans worked well and designed special pots for growing the mould. In 1941 the team treated a policeman, Albert Alexander, whose face was badly infected. He began to recover, but the supply ran out, and he died. Only after large-scale production began in Britain and the United States did penicillin become widely available.
下一個難題，是製造足夠給人用的分量。生化學家諾曼．希特利發現，形狀像醫院便盆的容器效果很好，於是設計了專門培養黴菌的陶罐。1941 年，團隊治療了臉部嚴重感染的警察艾伯特．亞歷山大。他開始康復，但藥用完了，他最後還是過世。直到英國和美國開始大規模生產之後，青黴素才得以普及。

In 1945, Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Popular memory, however, often reduces the story to a single lucky moment. In reality, the mould on Fleming’s dish became a medicine only through more than a decade of patient work by many people. Chance may start a discovery, but it rarely finishes one.
1945 年，弗萊明、弗洛里和柴恩共同獲得諾貝爾生理學或醫學獎。然而，大眾記憶常把這個故事簡化成一個幸運的瞬間。實際上，弗萊明培養皿上的黴菌，是靠許多人十多年耐心的努力，才變成了藥物。機緣或許能開啟一項發現，卻很少能完成它。

advanced.title: Serendipity Is Only the Beginning
paras: The discovery of penicillin is usually told as a parable of serendipity. On 3 September 1928, Alexander Fleming returned from a holiday in Suffolk to his laboratory at St Mary’s Hospital, London, and noticed that a culture plate of staphylococci had been contaminated by a fungus; the bacterial colonies immediately surrounding it had been destroyed. Fleming himself later reflected that “one sometimes finds what one is not looking for”. The anecdote is accurate as far as it goes. What it omits is how close the discovery came to having no practical consequence at all.
青黴素的發現，通常被講成一則關於機緣巧合的寓言。1928 年 9 月 3 日，亞歷山大．弗萊明從薩福克度假回到倫敦聖瑪麗醫院的實驗室，注意到一個葡萄球菌培養皿被真菌污染了；緊鄰真菌的細菌菌落都被消滅了。弗萊明後來回想道：「人有時會找到自己並沒有在找的東西。」這則軼事就其本身而言是準確的。它遺漏的是：這項發現差一點就完全沒有實際影響。

Fleming named the active substance penicillin on 7 March 1929 and reported his findings in the British Journal of Experimental Pathology, but the article attracted little notice. He was uncertain about the substance’s therapeutic potential and more interested in its use for isolating bacteria in the laboratory. Contrary to a persistent claim, he did not abandon the work — his notebooks show attempts to improve production as late as 1939 — but neither he nor his collaborators succeeded in isolating and purifying penicillin in usable quantities.
弗萊明在 1929 年 3 月 7 日把這種有效物質命名為青黴素，並在《英國實驗病理學期刊》發表研究結果，但文章幾乎沒有引起注意。他不確定這種物質的治療潛力，反而更關心它在實驗室分離細菌上的用途。與一個流傳已久的說法相反，他並沒有放棄這項研究——他的筆記顯示，直到 1939 年他仍在嘗試改進生產——但他和合作者都未能把青黴素分離、純化到可用的分量。

The transformation began in 1939 at the Sir William Dunn School of Pathology in Oxford, where a team led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain, including Norman Heatley, Edward Abraham and Margaret Jennings, developed methods to cultivate the mould, extract and store penicillin, and assay its purity. On 25 May 1940, Florey injected eight mice with a virulent strain of Streptococcus and treated four of them. By the early hours of the next day all four untreated mice were dead, while all four treated mice were alive. Florey called it “a miracle”.
轉變始於 1939 年牛津的威廉．鄧恩爵士病理學院。由霍華德．弗洛里和恩斯特．柴恩帶領、成員包括諾曼．希特利、愛德華．亞伯拉罕和瑪格麗特．詹寧斯的團隊，發展出培養黴菌、萃取並保存青黴素，以及檢測其純度的方法。1940 年 5 月 25 日，弗洛里給八隻老鼠注射強毒性的鏈球菌，再治療其中四隻。到了隔天凌晨，四隻未治療的老鼠全部死亡，四隻接受治療的則都還活著。弗洛里稱之為「奇蹟」。

Scaling up proved far harder than proving efficacy. Heatley, realising that vessels shaped like hospital bedpans were ideal for culturing the mould, designed ceramic versions that turned the Oxford laboratory into the first penicillin factory. Even so, supplies were desperately limited. In 1941 an Oxford policeman, Albert Alexander, who was suffering from a severe facial infection, improved dramatically under treatment; penicillin was even recovered from his urine to be reused, yet it was not enough, and he relapsed and died. Industrial production in Britain and the United States, driven by the demands of the Second World War, eventually made the drug widely available.
擴大生產遠比證明療效困難。希特利發現，形狀像醫院便盆的容器最適合培養黴菌，於是設計了陶瓷版本，把牛津實驗室變成了第一座青黴素工廠。即便如此，供應依然極度短缺。1941 年，一位臉部嚴重感染的牛津警察艾伯特．亞歷山大在治療下大幅好轉；研究人員甚至從他的尿液中回收青黴素重複使用，卻仍然不夠，他病情復發而過世。在第二次世界大戰需求的推動下，英國和美國的工業化生產最終讓這種藥物普及開來。

The 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was shared by Fleming, Florey and Chain, yet public memory has largely preserved only the first chapter. That selective memory distorts how discovery works. Fleming’s observation was necessary, but it was the patient, collaborative and often unglamorous labour of chemists, pathologists and technicians that converted a curiosity on a culture plate into what has been called the “single greatest victory ever achieved over disease”. Serendipity can open a door; it takes sustained effort to walk through it.
1945 年的諾貝爾生理學或醫學獎由弗萊明、弗洛里和柴恩共享，然而大眾記憶大多只保留了第一章。這種選擇性的記憶，扭曲了我們對「發現」如何發生的理解。弗萊明的觀察是必要的，但真正把培養皿上的一個奇特現象，轉化成被稱為「人類戰勝疾病最偉大的一場勝利」的，是化學家、病理學家和技術人員耐心、合作，而且往往毫不光鮮的勞動。機緣能打開一扇門；要走過去，靠的是持續的努力。

quote.text: One sometimes finds what one is not looking for.
quote.author: Alexander Fleming
quote.work: As quoted in the Wikipedia article “Alexander Fleming”

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Alexander Fleming spent his holiday in Scotland.
How a lucky discovery became a medicine through teamwork.
Why mice are better than people for testing medicine.
How to grow mould in hospital bedpans at home.
beginner.evidence: Great discoveries often need both luck and teamwork.
traps: 捏造：文中沒說他去哪裡度假。
捏造：文中沒有比較。
捏造：便盆形狀的罐子是牛津團隊的工具。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “Florey called it “a miracle”” refer to?
options: The Nobel Prize in 1945.
The mould on Fleming’s dish.
The science journal Fleming wrote for.
The result of the test on eight mice.
beginner.evidence: The four mice with penicillin were still alive the next day.
beginner.why: 前一句：用了盤尼西林的四隻老鼠活下來，這個結果被稱為奇蹟。
traps: 時序錯置：諾貝爾獎是 1945 年。
時序錯置：黴菌是 1928 年的事。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：期刊沒什麼人注意。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The policeman got better but died when the drug ran out.
Fleming made enough pure penicillin for many patients.
All eight of the mice in the test were given penicillin.
Fleming won the Nobel Prize in 1945 by himself.
beginner.evidence: He started to get better, but they ran out of penicillin, and he died.
traps: 正反顛倒：他無法做出足夠的純盤尼西林。
數字錯位：只有四隻接受治療。
正反顛倒：三人共同獲獎。

beginner.q: What does the 1942 example show about penicillin at that time?
options: It was used mainly for mice.
It was cheap and easy to buy.
It was still extremely scarce.
It was made only in Oxford.
beginner.evidence: one of the first American patients treated with penicillin used half of all the penicillin made in the country at that time
beginner.why: 一位病人就用掉全美一半的產量，可見極度稀少。
traps: 時序錯置：老鼠實驗是 1940 年。
正反顛倒：一人就用掉全美一半，可見藥量極少。
正反顛倒：這是在美國的例子。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Guinea pigs were used in the first successful tests.
Fleming gave up penicillin soon after discovering it.
Penicillin needed years of team effort after Fleming’s lucky discovery.
The policeman Albert Alexander was fully cured in 1941.
intermediate.evidence: the mould on Fleming’s dish became a medicine only through more than a decade of patient work by many people
traps: 正反顛倒：用的是老鼠，天竺鼠對盤尼西林有毒。
正反顛倒：原文 Fleming did not abandon the work。
正反顛倒：藥用完，他死了。

intermediate.q: What does “stalled” in the second paragraph most likely mean?
options: Stopped making progress.
Became very famous.
Moved to another country.
Was proved to be wrong.
intermediate.why: 後面說論文沒人理、無法純化，可知是「停滯不前」。
traps: 正反顛倒：論文幾乎沒人注意。
捏造：突破來自牛津，但發現本身沒「搬家」。
正反顛倒：發現是對的，只是進展停住。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Florey gave penicillin to all eight mice.
Fleming named penicillin in September 1928.
Heatley was the policeman treated in 1941.
Penicillin is toxic to guinea pigs.
intermediate.evidence: penicillin is toxic to guinea pigs
traps: 數字錯位：只給了四隻。
數字錯位：1929 年 3 月 7 日命名。
張冠李戴：Heatley 是生化學家，警察是 Albert Alexander。

intermediate.q: Why was the Oxford team “lucky in its choice of animals”?
options: Mice were cheaper than any other animal.
Testing on guinea pigs might have stopped the research.
The mice had already been treated by Fleming.
Guinea pigs could not catch the bacteria.
intermediate.evidence: penicillin is toxic to guinea pigs, so testing on them might have stopped the research
traps: 捏造：文中沒提價格。
張冠李戴：Fleming 沒有做動物實驗。
捏造：問題在盤尼西林對天竺鼠有毒。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain how bacteria become resistant to modern drugs.
To prove that Fleming’s discovery was not really an accident.
To describe the Second World War and its battles in detail.
To show that the popular story leaves out years of teamwork.
advanced.evidence: That selective memory distorts how discovery works.
advanced.why: 最後一段：大眾只記得第一章，扭曲了科學發現的實況。
traps: 捏造：文中沒談抗藥性。
正反顛倒：作者承認這是意外。
以偏概全：二戰只是量產的推力。

advanced.q: What does “serendipity” in the first paragraph most likely mean?
options: Careful planning over many years.
Finding something valuable by chance.
Working closely with other scientists.
Losing an important discovery.
advanced.evidence: Fleming himself later reflected that “one sometimes finds what one is not looking for”.
advanced.why: 後面引言：有時找到的不是自己在找的東西，也就是意外的好運。
traps: 正反顛倒：這是後來團隊的長期努力。
張冠李戴：團隊合作是作者認為被忽略的部分。
正反顛倒：發現差點沒有成果，但沒有遺失。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Florey’s team at Oxford included only two scientists.
Fleming was mainly interested in penicillin as a medicine.
Fleming’s notebooks show work on production as late as 1939.
Heatley’s ceramic vessels were shaped like small test tubes.
advanced.evidence: his notebooks show attempts to improve production as late as 1939
traps: 數字錯位：團隊還有 Heatley、Abraham、Jennings 等人。
正反顛倒：他更有興趣用它分離細菌。
捏造：是像醫院便盆的形狀。

advanced.q: What does the recovery of penicillin from a patient’s urine suggest?
options: Supplies were so limited that it had to be reused.
Penicillin worked much better after it had been reused.
The patient did not really need any more penicillin.
Industrial production had already started in Britain by then.
advanced.evidence: Even so, supplies were desperately limited.
advanced.why: 第四段：藥量少到要從尿液回收再用。
traps: 捏造：文中沒有。重點是數量不足。
正反顛倒：他病情改善，但藥不夠而死。
時序錯置：工業化生產是後來的事。

reflections: Why do you think people remember Fleming’s lucky moment more than the Oxford team’s years of work?
Think of a success in your own life. How much came from luck, and how much from steady effort?

Contrary to a popular claim, he did not abandon the work—his notebooks show attempts to improve production as late as 1939. Yet neither he nor his collaborators managed to purify penicillin in usable amounts.
弗萊明在 1929 年 3 月 7 日把這種活性物質命名為盤尼西林，並發表在《英國實驗病理學期刊》，但文章幾乎沒人注意。他不確定它當藥有多少價值，反而比較想用它在實驗室裡分離細菌。和流行的說法相反，他沒有放棄——筆記顯示他直到 1939 年還在嘗試改良產量。但他和合作者都沒能提煉出可用份量的純盤尼西林。

It was in Oxford, not London, that the turning point came. Starting in 1939, a team led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed methods to grow the mould, extract penicillin, and measure its purity. On 25 May 1940, Florey infected eight mice with a deadly strain of bacteria and treated four of them. By early the next morning, all four untreated mice were dead, while all four treated ones were alive—a result Florey called “a miracle.”
轉折點出現在牛津，而不是倫敦。從 1939 年起，弗洛里和柴恩帶領的團隊發展出培養黴菌、萃取盤尼西林、測量純度的方法。1940 年 5 月 25 日，弗洛里讓八隻老鼠感染致命細菌，並治療其中四隻。隔天清晨，四隻沒治療的全死了，四隻治療過的都活著——弗洛里稱之為「奇蹟」。

Producing enough of the drug for humans, however, proved far harder than proving that it worked. Norman Heatley, a member of the team, realized that vessels shaped like hospital bedpans were ideal for growing the mould, and his ceramic versions turned the Oxford laboratory into the first penicillin factory. Even so, supplies were so limited that penicillin was recovered from a patient’s urine to be reused. That patient, a policeman named Albert Alexander, improved dramatically under treatment, but the supply was not enough, and he relapsed and died. Not until industrial production began in Britain and the United States, driven by the demands of the Second World War, did the drug become widely available.
然而要生產足夠給人用的藥，比證明它有效難得多。團隊成員諾曼・希特利發現形狀像醫院便盆的容器最適合培養黴菌，他做的陶瓷版本把牛津實驗室變成第一座盤尼西林工廠。即使如此，藥量少到必須從病人的尿液回收盤尼西林再用。那位病人是警察亞伯特・亞歷山大，他在治療下大幅好轉，但藥量不夠，病情復發而死。直到英美在二戰需求推動下展開工業化生產，盤尼西林才普及。

In 1945, Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Popular memory, however, has largely preserved only the first chapter of the story. Fleming’s observation was necessary, but it was years of patient, collaborative work by chemists, pathologists and technicians that turned a curiosity on a dish into a life-saving medicine. Chance may open a door; it takes sustained effort to walk through it.
1945 年，弗萊明、弗洛里和柴恩共同獲得諾貝爾生理醫學獎。然而大眾記憶大多只保留了故事的第一章。弗萊明的觀察固然必要，但把培養皿上的奇特現象變成救命藥物的，是化學家、病理學家和技術人員多年耐心的合作。機運也許能打開一扇門，要走過去卻得靠持續的努力。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that Fleming’s discovery was not really an accident.
To show that turning a lucky discovery into a medicine took many people’s effort.
To explain why Fleming gave up his research on penicillin.
To describe how penicillin saved soldiers during the Second World War.
questions.evidence: it was years of patient, collaborative work by chemists, pathologists and technicians
questions.why: 第一段提出「這個故事少說了什麼」，第二到五段說明從發現到藥物靠的是許多人多年的合作。
traps: 正反顛倒：文中承認是意外（finds what one is not looking for），重點在意外之後。
正反顛倒：原文 Contrary to a popular claim, he did not abandon the work。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：二戰只用來說明工業生產的推力，文中沒寫救了士兵。

questions.q: What does “the first chapter of the story” in the last paragraph refer to?
options: Fleming’s chance discovery in 1928.
The Oxford team’s experiment on mice.
The earliest article published about penicillin.
The Nobel Prize awarded in 1945.
questions.evidence: Popular memory, however, has largely preserved only the first chapter of the story.
questions.why: 大眾只記得「幸運的開頭」，也就是 1928 年的意外發現；下一句 Fleming’s observation was necessary 也在呼應。
traps: 時序錯置：老鼠實驗是 1940 年的轉折點，不是開頭。
字面誤讀：把 chapter 理解成真正的出版品；1929 年的文章也不是故事的起點。
時序錯置：諾貝爾獎是故事的結尾。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Fleming’s 1929 article quickly attracted the attention of other scientists.
Florey treated all eight mice, and all of them survived.
Albert Alexander was the first patient to be fully cured by penicillin.
Penicillin was so scarce that some of it was collected and used again.
questions.evidence: supplies were so limited that penicillin was recovered from a patient’s urine to be reused
questions.why: 正解把 recovered … to be reused 改寫成 collected and used again，so limited 改寫成 so scarce。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 attracted little notice。
數字錯位：八隻只治療四隻，活下來的是治療過的四隻。
正反顛倒：他好轉後又 relapsed and died。

questions.q: Here is a sentence: “The question was no longer whether penicillin worked, but how to make enough of it.” Which paragraph is most suitable to have it as the final sentence?
options: Paragraph 1.
Paragraph 2.
Paragraph 3.
Paragraph 4.
questions.evidence: all four treated ones were alive—a result Florey called “a miracle.”
questions.why: 第三段結尾的老鼠實驗證明「有效」，第四段開頭就講「量產比證明有效更難」，這句正好銜接兩段。
traps: 時序錯置：第一段時還不知道它有沒有效。
時序錯置：第二段的問題是「純化不出來」，還沒證明有效。
位置陷阱：第四段已經在講量產，而且最後一句已經講到普及，再放這句就重複了。

mixed.prompt: Fleming’s article on penicillin attracted little [47], and it took years of patient, [48] work by many people to turn his discovery into a medicine.
mixed.why: 第一格出自第二段 attracted little notice；第二格出自第五段 patient, collaborative work（第二段的 collaborators 是名詞，這裡要用形容詞）。

mixed.q: Which of the following were done by the Oxford team? Choose ALL that apply.
options: Developing methods to grow the mould and measure its purity.
First noticing that the mould destroyed bacteria.
Testing penicillin on infected mice.
Making ceramic vessels for growing the mould.
Naming the substance penicillin.
Starting industrial production in the United States.
mixed.why: A、C 第三段；D 第四段。B、E 張冠李戴（是弗萊明）；F 張冠李戴（是英美的工業化生產，不是牛津團隊）。
